main_body: Altar block: a white upper area with a purple cloth and gold cross, over a purple front panel with a gold cross, on a grey stone step
top_band: White, rows 11-23, with a lilac cloth panel and cross that read as a vertical hanging. A gold band at rows 24-25 and a brown row at 26 follow. No clear foreshortened horizontal surface.
evidence: The upper white zone carries an upright cross and cloth drawn face-on, so it is a vertical face (a retable or frontal) stacked above the purple front, not a top surface. The only real horizontal marker is the 2px gold band plus a 1px brown line. The purple front has vertical stripes painted flat with no inset shadow. Two stacked front panels with a thin gold band make a front elevation, not a 3/4 box.

style.evidence: The white block is a large flat fill with no grain. The purple front has about 3 tones in vertical stripes and the cross is a flat gold shape. The stone step is a few grey bands. There is no texture or speckle, and per-tile colour counts are far below the stall and well references. It looks thinner and flatter than they do.
